description:
FILED s440 from agent B's #466 report (pre-existing). The dup modes `>&`, `<&`, `>&=`, `<&=` with a glob ref, a bareword (`open(F, ">&STDOUT")`), a lexical handle and a numeric fd must create a second handle on the same stream (write-through, close independent). Bar: each spelling vs perl (output interleaving through both handles; `close $dup` leaves STDOUT open); a Pl/t guard row in fileio-01.t or the open topical file; a perl-shaped failure for an unknown source handle.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 7ea827a6) ===
VERDICT: NARROWED -- the filed failure ("fails in every spelling") is gone; the output ORDER of an fdopen'ed handle differs.
PASS (= perl 5.40.3): `open($fh, ">&", \*STDOUT)` + `print $fh` / `print {$fh}` ; `close $fh` leaves STDOUT open ;
  `open(F, ">&STDOUT")` ; `open($g, ">&", STDOUT)` ; `open($k, ">&", fileno(STDOUT))` ; `open($l, ">&", $h)` (a lexical) ; each
  dup's output buffered like perl's relative to an autoflushed STDOUT.  (perl-suite-run.tsv's s4xx note: "#513 fixed the TEN dup
  rows" of io/open.t -- the task was not closed then.)
FAILS (silent, ordering):
    $| = 1;
    open(my $m, ">&=1") or die; print $m "A via >&=1\n"; print "B STDOUT\n";
    open(my $n, ">&=", 1) or die; print $n "C via >&=, 1\n"; print "D STDOUT\n";
    perl: B, D, ..., C, A (the fdopen handles have their OWN buffers, flushed at exit)
    PCL : A, B, C, D, ... (the line appears at once: the handle shares STDOUT's stream and its $|)
  The `>&` (dup) spelling buffers separately in PCL too, so only `>&=` is affected.
ALSO SEEN (not this task's): `open($bad, ">&", "NOSUCHHANDLE")` dies "Bad filehandle: NOSUCHHANDLE" in both, but perl exits 25 (the
  leftover errno, ENOTTY) and PCL 255 -- the die-exit-status-from-$! family (#2740 is one spelling of it).
LABEL: silent (subject rewritten to the residue).

subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): a `>&=` (fdopen) handle on STDOUT shares STDOUT's buffer in PCL -- with $| = 1 its lines come out at once, where perl buffers them in the new handle until exit; every dup spelling itself works (the filed failure is fixed)
